title: Non-Parametric Hypothesis Testing
description: Rank-based hypothesis testing for comparing distributions when normality assumptions are violated.
conditions: Small sample sizes (N < 30 per group) or severe non-normality and skewness
recommended_methods: Mann-Whitney U test (Wilcoxon Rank-Sum) for two independent groups
Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test for paired dependent samples
Kruskal-Wallis H test for three or more independent groups
selection_rules: If outcome distribution is skewed or ordinal, select Mann-Whitney U over t-test
If testing three or more non-normal groups, execute Kruskal-Wallis followed by Dunn's post-hoc test with Bonferroni correction
If group distributions have identical shapes, Mann-Whitney tests medians; otherwise, it tests stochastic dominance
limitations: Lower statistical power than t-tests when normality actually holds (~95% asymptotic relative efficiency)
Tied ranks require continuity correction in small samples
source: Mann and Whitney (1947) Test of Whether One of Two Variables is Stochastically Larger
